bug_semantics: A normal authenticated Ech0 user can retrieve historical application logs with GET /api/system/logs and subscribe to live logs over SSE at /api/system/logs/stream or WebSocket at /ws/system/logs. The HTTP routes originally required only a valid JWT, the WS group had no authorization middleware, the stream handlers merely parsed the supplied JWT, and the dashboard service read or streamed the log backend without an administrator-role or privileged-scope check. Consequently a low-privilege session reaches operational data such as paths, stack traces, internal URLs, and admin/background activity.
flaw_origin: fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333 introduced the complete flawed mechanism in one feature commit: internal/router/dashboard.go added all three /system/logs routes without an admin gate; internal/handler/dashboard/dashboard.go added GetSystemLogs, SSESubscribeSystemLogs, and WSSubscribeSystemLogs with no role check beyond token validity; and internal/service/dashboard/dashboard.go added direct log query/stream methods with no compensating authorization. At that commit, internal/router/router.go applied JWTAuthMiddleware only to AuthRouterGroup and left WSRouterGroup as a bare /ws group.
ai_marker: absent — the exact fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333 commit object has author and committer 'L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com>' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-cp79-9mwr-wr49 and its repository API record https://api.github.com/repos/lin-snow/Ech0/security-advisories/GHSA-cp79-9mwr-wr49 identify CWE-862, the three endpoints, the normal-user PoC, affected range <=4.3.4, and patched version 4.4.3; the assigned alias is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7j6f-2mq2-g5vq. `git log -L 7,9:internal/router/dashboard.go 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313^` traces all three vulnerable route lines to fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333, and `git log --all -SGetSystemLogs` finds no earlier source introduction. At the BIC, `git grep -n` locates routes at internal/router/dashboard.go:8-9,11, handlers at internal/handler/dashboard/dashboard.go:87,120,149, and service methods at internal/service/dashboard/dashboard.go:80,88,151. `git grep` of direct parent 51690dd61a629f7a0f1728583c6de55282699e70 for /system/logs, GetSystemLogs, SSESubscribeSystemLogs, WSSubscribeSystemLogs, SystemLogQuery, and QueryLogFileTail returns no matches, proving parent-tree absence. Commit URL: https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333. Tag membership shows v3.1.4 does not contain the BIC, while v4.0.0 (commit 93b935c5b64020c7475abb9df071fdf8663b9f84) is the first v4 release and contains all three routes; v4.3.4 contains them as advertised. v4.4.2 (commit 7b7890cbe294659df39c36feb51fcfbe9ec9bdb2) still has all three unscoped route registrations. `git log v4.4.2..v4.4.3 -- internal/router/dashboard.go` identifies 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 as the direct attempted fix, and `git tag --contains` first places it in v4.4.3 (commit b934467d26b91c96dc7c937b6a4e47d8d01484eb); fix-attempt URL: https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313. Its diff adds RequireScopes(ScopeAdminSettings) only to GET and SSE, leaving the WS route unscoped. Moreover internal/middleware/scope.go:17-21 at that commit explicitly calls ctx.Next() for every TokenTypeSession, and internal/util/jwt/jwt.go:24-34 creates TokenTypeSession claims for ordinary login tokens, so the advisory's normal-user session still bypasses the new middleware. No service-layer admin check was added. The same WS registration and session bypass remain at audited HEAD 5ce1dd0a3d7092be537fb309a8685d024e8986de. Thus 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 is recorded as the direct partial/advertised fix evidence, not as proof of complete remediation; tags v4.3.5 through v4.4.2 are also vulnerable despite being omitted between the advisory's <=4.3.4 cap and claimed 4.4.3 patch.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle begins in fcbe5084a4f095760ac691039ef1999ce50db333, not in a later move or refactor: that one-parent feature commit first created the externally reachable routes, permissive handlers, and unauthorizing service methods together. Line history and the all-ref string search converge on that commit, while direct inspection of its immediate parent 51690dd61a629f7a0f1728583c6de55282699e70 proves the endpoint names, handler symbols, query type, and log-tail call were absent. There is no reconstructable squash/member history to decompose. Release ancestry bounds introduction between unaffected v3.1.4 and affected v4.0.0 and confirms the mechanism through v4.4.2. Although the first-party advisory declares 4.4.3 patched and that tag contains 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313, source review shows only a partial access-token mitigation: WebSocket remains untouched, session tokens are expressly exempted by RequireScopes, and the recommended defense-in-depth service check is absent. Therefore the issue is still unpatched for the advisory's normal authenticated-user attack path. Attribution is nevertheless closed: only the BIC commit object controls the AI judgment, and its human author/committer plus complete absence of AI trailers or bot markers supports NOT_AI; later AI-marked refactors are irrelevant and were not used for attribution.
remaining_gap: Unpatched implementation gap, not an evidence gap: no complete fix exists in the audited public history through 5ce1dd0a3d7092be537fb309a8685d024e8986de. The advertised/direct partial fix 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 leaves /ws/system/logs without ScopeAdminSettings, exempts all session tokens from the added scope middleware on GET/SSE, and adds no service-layer administrator check. A complete fix SHA and genuinely fixed release boundary therefore do not yet exist.
